assumptions: Two 12 m gables rise to 8.4 m. Fixed-base paired channels. A 12 m by 8 m independently braced mezzanine at +3.5 m occupies the west span at the south end.
Levels, member axes and all dimensions in the handoff are in millimetres. Verify site soil, opening ratios, terrain, heat numbers and supplier data.

Physical framing uses nominal analytic workpoints and untrimmed member ends. Panels follow structural control planes. Coordinate finish buildups, offsets, coping and weld preparations in fabrication details.
The native design gate and governing member checks travel with this model. Review open primary-frame, concrete, diaphragm and fastening checks before design acceptance.
Any proposed in-plane board stiffness and allowable shear require full assembly test evidence. Concrete pedestal and group breakout design must be verified.
Dead loads are preliminary assembly allowances. No imposed-load reduction is used. Primary member self-weight is computed separately by the solver.

Mezzanine posts begin 0.7 m inside the portal lines. A 12 m floor plate spans four 2.65 m bays and two 0.7 m end cantilevers. The native design envelopes 3 m joist spans. The independent foundations retain 50 mm clear between adjacent 650 mm plates.

Hyderabad paired-channel flanges have positive restraint at maximum 1200 mm along the analytical member. Interior posts have longitudinal rails and end-bay X-bracing. Apply project restraint reactions to the final cladding support and foundations.

Native levels are analytic structural worklines. Floor joists bear on girder flanges; roof purlins bear through their detailed seats. The issued board or roof skin starts on the upper flange. Supplier floor retention, deck fasteners and the podium deck/slab specification remain project inputs.

Pitched purlins sit on the modeled seats, with 75 mm workpoint setbacks on both sides of roof folds. Roof surfaces retain the architectural ridge and eave plan coordinates. Supplier flashing, ridge and valley closures, roof and gable transition, screw patterns, waterproofing and tolerances require coordination.
